title: Cherry-Oak Lamb with Orange-Mint Gravy
description: Lean lamb leg slices replace fatty shoulder and are served in a fragrant orange gravy finished with fresh mint.
equipment: Small enamel Dutch oven with tight lid, sized to hold the food snugly

ingredients.name: lean boneless lamb leg steak
ingredients.note: Use an intact muscle and trim away all the outer fat and silver skin.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Use plain broth made from meat, bones and water, with no added vegetable blend or seasonings.

ingredients.name: fresh orange peel
ingredients.note: A thin strip without white pith; remove before serving.

ingredients.name: hot drinking water
ingredients.note: Keep ready; use only as needed to maintain liquid depth or make up the sauce measure.

steps.title: Heat the Traeger
steps.text: Preheat the Traeger Silverton 610 to 275°F with cherry and oak, mixed in equal parts pellets, about 15 minutes with the lid closed.

steps.title: Warm the braising liquid
steps.text: Bring {broth} with {peel}, {cumin} and {coriander} just to a simmer in the open Dutch oven on the stove, about 3–6 minutes.

steps.title: Smoke the braising liquid
steps.text: Move the uncovered pot to the Traeger grate. Close the smoker lid and smoke the liquid for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Slice the lamb
steps.text: Find the grain in {lamb} and cut across it into 1/3-inch slices.

steps.title: Cover to poach
steps.text: Nestle the lamb in the hot liquid in a single layer. Add {topup} to just cover if needed, and fit the lid immediately. No stall wrap is needed.

steps.title: Check the lamb
steps.text: Poach covered at 275°F for 7–18 minutes, checking each thick center sideways from 7 minutes. Transfer portions at 145°F to a covered bowl with a spoonful of broth.

steps.title: Rest in the juices
steps.text: Rest the covered lamb off heat for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Remove the peel
steps.text: Lift the strip of peel out of the broth and discard it.

steps.title: Measure the sauce base
steps.text: Skim excess fat from the braising liquid. Measure 3/4 cup into the HexClad skillet, topping up with {topup} if needed.

steps.title: Add the orange
steps.text: Whisk {orange} into the juices over medium heat.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the skillet liquid to a boil. Whisk in the stirred slurry and simmer for 1 minute, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Finish with mint
steps.text: Stir {mint} into the gravy off heat. Divide the lamb between warm bowls and cover it with the mint gravy.

notes: Make ahead: Slice the lamb while well chilled and keep covered in the refrigerator. Option A uses orange and mint. For gentler Option B, replace the orange juice with broth, omit the peel and substitute parsley for mint. Refrigerate promptly in shallow portions and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze individual portions surrounded by sauce for up to 2 months to protect their moisture. Fridge reheat: Warm one portion covered in its sauce in the HexClad over medium-low heat. Turn gently, adding a splash of water if needed. Check after 6 minutes and continue until the food reaches 165°F throughout. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator. Follow the fridge reheating directions and stir the sauce smooth. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 200 kcal, 30.3 g protein, 3.5 g total carbohydrate, 6.5 g fat, 0.2 g fiber, 109 mg sodium. Includes the measured broth and sauce. Sodium varies with your broth.
